source.title_on_document: IMPLEMENTASI PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA BERBANTUAN GEMINI.AI TERHADAP PENINGKATAN KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KREATIF DAN ADVERSITY QUOTIENT SISWA

paper_design_summary: Quasi-experiment (pretest-posttest control group design) at one private senior high school in Medan, Indonesia. Two intact grade-10 classes were chosen by purposive sampling: class X-2 (35 students) received mathematics instruction assisted by Gemini.AI on systems of two-variable linear equations (SPLDV), and class X-3 (35 students) received conventional instruction, over 18 days with three meetings per week. The paper compares N-gain on a 5-item creative-thinking test (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) and on a 32-item adversity-quotient questionnaire with independent-sample t-tests.

studies.label: Grade-10 mathematics classes, Gemini.AI-assisted vs conventional instruction

assignment.what_was_assigned: Intact classes selected by purposive sampling: class X-2 became the experimental class (Gemini.AI-assisted mathematics instruction), class X-3 the control class (conventional instruction).
assignment.quote: pengambilan sampel dalam penelitian ini dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling ... Sehingga, diperoleh kelas X-3 yaitu sebagai kelas kontrol dan kelas X-2 sebagai kelas eksperimen

arms.name: Kelas eksperimen (X-2)
arms.description: Mathematics instruction assisted by Gemini.AI (pembelajaran matematika berbantuan AI), SPLDV material

arms.name: Kelas kontrol (X-3)
arms.description: Conventional mathematics instruction (pembelajaran konvensional), no treatment

participants.who: Grade-10 (kelas X) students at SMA Swasta Budi Satrya Medan, school year 2024/2025; population of 4 classes, 135 students; 2 classes (35 + 35) sampled. The t-test df of 68 matches 70 students analyzed.
participants.quote: diperoleh kelas X-3 yaitu sebagai kelas kontrol dan kelas X-2 sebagai kelas eksperimen dengan jumlah siswa pada kelas eksperimen sebanyak 35 siswa dan pada kelas kontrol sebanyak 35 siswa.
participants.locator: PDF pp. 5-6 (journal pp. 189-190), Metode; abstract PDF p. 1

ai_tool.how_used: The paper says only that the experimental class had mathematics instruction assisted by Gemini.AI, designed as a series of engaging and interactive activities (PDF p. 10, journal p. 194). It does not describe how students or the teacher used Gemini, or whether Gemini was available during the posttest.

task.description: Classroom mathematics instruction on systems of two-variable linear equations (SPLDV). Creative thinking was measured with a 5-item test built on fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration indicators, given as pretest and posttest.
task.duration: 18 days, three meetings per week in each class (PDF p. 6, journal p. 190)

outcomes.name: Creative-thinking test (kemampuan berpikir kreatif), N-gain from pretest to posttest
outcomes.measure_detail: 5-item test on fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration (Filsaime 2008; Maysarah 2018); validated with product-moment correlation and Cronbach alpha. Who scored the answers and the rubric are not stated. N-gain = gain over maximum possible gain.

contrasts.reported: Mean N-gain experimental 61,65% (0,617) vs control 50,42% (0,504), both 'sedang' category. Independent-samples t-test on N-gain (Table 4, equal variances assumed): t = -2.1, df = 68, Sig. (2-tailed) = .04 (text: 0,041), mean difference = -.112, std. error difference = .054; Levene F = 2.1, Sig. = .15. Equal variances not assumed: t = -2.1, df = 66.3, Sig. = .04. Arm SDs of the creativity scores are not reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 1 (journal p. 185), Abstrak: decimal N-gains 0,617 and 0,504; PDF p. 8 (journal p. 192), Uji N-Gain: 61,65% and 50,42%, both sedang; PDF p. 9 (journal p. 193), Table 4: t-tests, Levene test, mean difference and standard error; paragraph immediately below Table 4: p = 0,041.

eligibility.reason: Two intact classes were selected by purposive sampling; random assignment of students, classes or condition order is not reported (PDF pp. 5-6, journal pp. 189-190, Metode and Table 1), so criterion 1 is not met. The study analyzed 70 students, 35 per class (PDF p. 1, Abstrak; PDF p. 7, Table 3; PDF p. 9, Table 4), meeting criterion 2. The creative-thinking outcome is scored on answers to a five-item test covering fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration (PDF p. 6, Metode), meeting criterion 3, although the scorer and scoring method are not identified. Test-time AI availability and assessment timing are also not stated. The study remains non-core observational context.

one_line_finding: In a non-random two-class comparison of 70 grade-10 students (PDF p. 1, Abstrak; PDF pp. 5-6, Metode), mean creative-thinking N-gain was 0,617 with Gemini.AI-assisted instruction versus 0,504 with conventional instruction (PDF p. 1, Abstrak), with t = -2.1, df = 68 and Sig. (2-tailed) = .04 (PDF p. 9, Table 4, equal variances assumed), while the paragraph below Table 4 reports p = 0,041.
notes: AI availability or removal during the posttest and the interval between instruction and assessment are not stated (PDF p. 6, journal p. 190, Metode and Table 1; full PDF reviewed), so question, ai_available_when_produced and timing are null. Chronological order alone does not establish after_ai. The creative-thinking test scorer and scoring method are not identified (PDF p. 6, instruments paragraph; full PDF reviewed). The second outcome, adversity quotient (32-item questionnaire, self-report, not creativity; PDF p. 6), is omitted from outcomes: N-gain 0,419 vs 0,337 (PDF p. 1, Abstrak), t = -3.3, df = 68, Sig. = .001 (Table 5, PDF p. 9); Table 2 (PDF p. 7) descriptives refer to this questionnaire only. Internal inconsistency: the text on PDF p. 8 gives Shapiro-Wilk Sig. 0,846 for the experimental class and 0,62 for the control class, while Table 3 (PDF p. 7) shows .846 for the control class and .062 for the experimental class. The abstract (PDF p. 1) reports creative-thinking N-gain as 0,617 and 0,504; Uji N-Gain (PDF p. 8) reports 61,65% and 50,42%.
